description: Access requirements, not a provider-specific executable rule. Configure and test the corresponding CloudBase rules before enabling uploads.

prefixes.purpose: immutable server copy for content review
approved post images, video and derived media; visibility enforced by service
prefixes.cleanup: deleted post or abandoned unreferenced upload

requiredChecks: user A cannot overwrite or delete user B incoming uploads
users A and B cannot modify/read quarantine objects
users A and B cannot modify/delete server-published objects
deletion and repeated deletion are handled correctly
ordinary clients cannot directly read published objects or create temporary URLs for them, even when they know a file ID
only an authorized post viewer or the owner of an unpublished upload receives a signed media URL

before setting PUBLISHED_MEDIA_PRIVATE=true, verify in the deployed environment that an ordinary client cannot download or call getTempFileURL for a known published file ID, including when its post is otherwise readable
measure the deployed expiry of image, video, poster and cover URLs; requesting maxAge=60 does not establish the provider's actual TTL
removing a friendship or restricting post visibility rejects new media URLs; previously issued bearer URLs may continue working until the provider's actual expiry

publishedMediaAccess.scope: community/published/ only; preserve owner-only incoming-upload rules separately
publishedMediaAccess.authorization: Authorize the owning post (or unpublished upload owner) before every signing request; the adapter is not a client-callable action

providerTTL.verification: WeChat documents a ten-minute lifetime for private-file URLs while also accepting maxAge examples. The server SDK forwards the requested maxAge; neither that request nor unit tests prove the deployed expiry. Verify and record the actual provider TTL before enabling private media. Public-read file URLs may not expire.

publishedMediaAccess.failClosed: Do not return raw cloud file IDs or public URLs when signing is missing or fails
publishedMediaAccess.revocation: Deny all new URL issuance immediately; previously issued bearer URLs may remain usable until the provider's actual expiry. Revocation does not invalidate an already issued URL or recall downloaded media.
